chunks: Yunus, from Musanna, from Abu Baseer who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Abu Zarr, may Allah have mercy on him, was saying: O seeker of knowledge! Indeed, this tongue is a key for goodness and a key for evil. Therefore, set a seal upon your tongue just as you set a seal upon your gold and your silver.'
ai.seo_question: How should a seeker of knowledge guard their tongue according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the pivotal role of tongue-guarding in Shia ethical formation, linking the preservation of knowledge to the restraint of speech. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of securing gold and silver to emphasize that uncontrolled speech can lead to either great benefit or significant harm, a concept deeply rooted in the tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt. This advice underscores the practical application of 'hilm' (forbearance) as a prerequisite for true intellectual and spiritual growth.
